title: Sep 23 Results + Sep 24 Preview: A Perfectly Balanced Day (For Better or Worse)
summary: Sep 23 went 8-8 at 50%, but here's why tomorrow's Pirates-Cardinals pick has our attention

content.value:
## Here's the Thing About Going .500

So... we went 8-8 yesterday. Perfectly balanced, as all things should be? Maybe in theory. But here's the reality: a 50% day feels like standing on a tightrope. You didn't fall off, but you didn't exactly soar either.

The model had some beautiful moments—nailing three 60% confidence picks with the Yankees, Sox, and Braves. But it also stumbled on what should've been solid calls. The Tigers? The Pirates? Those misses sting a little more when you look back.

## The Highs and the Lows

Let's talk about what worked. Our higher confidence picks (60%) went 3-for-4, which is actually pretty solid. The Yankees took care of business against the Rays, the Sox handled the Guardians, and the Braves did what the Braves do against the Reds.

The Orioles sweep of their doubleheader against the Jays was chef's kiss—two picks, two wins, even if the confidence wasn't sky-high.

But then there were the head-scratchers. The Tigers loss when we had 60% confidence? Ouch. The Phillies couldn't get it done at home against the Brewers. And the Pirates... well, we'll get to them in a minute.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick: Running It Back in Pittsburgh

Here's where it gets interesting. After the Pirates didn't come through for us yesterday at 54% confidence, the model is... going right back to them. Cardinals vs. Pirates, take two.

The confidence is lower this time—just 51%—but there's a storyline here that's hard to ignore. Paul Skenes is on the mound for Pittsburgh. You know, the guy who's been one of the most electric young pitchers in baseball this season. Against Kyle Leahy for the Cardinals, who's... well, let's just say he's not Paul Skenes.

Is this the model believing in regression to the mean? Is it the pitching matchup? Maybe a little of both. At 51%, it's essentially a coin flip with a slight lean toward the home team and their ace.

## The Bottom Line

A .500 day isn't the end of the world—it's baseball, after all. These things happen. The good news? Our high-confidence picks mostly delivered. The challenge? Those mid-confidence picks are where things got messy.

Heading into Sep 24, we're keeping our expectations measured. A 51% pick isn't a screaming bet, but with Skenes on the mound, there's at least a compelling narrative.

Sometimes in baseball—and in predictions—you just have to trust the process and see what happens. Here's to a better day tomorrow. 🤞
